name: Hip and femur fracture fixation
description: Surgery to fix a broken hip or thigh bone with a nail, plate or screws (keeps the patient's own hip joint).

name: Primary hip and knee replacement
description: Elective total or partial hip or knee replacement, plus total ankle replacement, which CMS groups into the same DRGs. Medicare pays hip, knee and ankle under the same DRGs, so the data can't separate them.

name: Lumbar and thoracolumbar spinal fusion
description: Fusion of the lower or mid spine with screws, rods and cages, including combined front-and-back fusions and deformity cases.

name: Hip replacement for hip fracture
description: Replacing part or all of the hip joint after a hip fracture (hemiarthroplasty or total hip).

name: Revision hip and knee replacement
description: Redoing a hip or knee replacement: removing and replacing worn, loose or infected components.

name: Cervical spinal fusion
description: Fusion of the neck, most often an anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) with a cage and plate.

name: Leg and upper-arm fracture surgery
description: Fixing fractures of the knee, lower leg, ankle and upper arm (everything except hip, femur and foot) with plates, nails, screws and external fixators.

name: Shoulder and elbow replacement
description: Total, reverse and partial shoulder replacement, plus elbow replacement (one DRG covers both).

name: Spine surgery without fusion
description: Spine operations that don't fuse bones, such as decompression (laminectomy or discectomy) and laminoplasty. CMS groups disc devices and neurostimulators in DRG 518, and spine operations for nervous-system diagnoses in DRGs 28 to 30.

name: Other bone and joint surgery
description: Musculoskeletal operations that CMS doesn't place in a more specific group. The group mixes many unrelated operations, so OrthoParity links no device categories to it.

name: Debridement, biopsy and amputation
description: Wound debridement and skin grafts for bone and joint problems, bone and soft-tissue biopsies, and amputations. These operations rarely use implants. OrthoParity links one device category: antibiotic-eluting bone void filler, which CMS names in its amputation and biopsy DRGs starting in fiscal year 2027.

name: Knee surgery other than replacement
description: Knee operations other than joint replacement, such as ligament repair, meniscus surgery and surgery for a knee infection. Most of this surgery is now outpatient, so inpatient numbers are small.

name: Shoulder, elbow, forearm, hand and wrist surgery other than replacement
description: Fracture fixation, tendon and ligament repair of the shoulder, elbow, forearm, hand and wrist, other than joint replacement. Most of this surgery is now outpatient, so inpatient numbers are small.

name: Foot and soft-tissue surgery
description: Foot surgery (bunion, fusion and fracture fixation) and soft-tissue operations such as tendon repair. Most of this surgery is now outpatient, so inpatient numbers are small.

name: Removal of plates, screws and other fixation
description: Surgery to remove plates, screws, rods or pins outside the hip and femur. The operation takes implants out instead of putting them in, so OrthoParity links no device categories to it.
